findings.evidence: Lines 283-289: docstring vs `example (L : Subalgebra ℝ ℍ[ℝ]) (h : Module.finrank ℝ ↥L = 2) : L ≠ ⊥`. `exists_subalgebra_isField_finrank_eq_deg` applied to `D = K` gives `finrank K L = deg K K = 1`, i.e. `L = ⊥`.
findings.fix: Scope the claim: "...so when `deg K D > 1` the maximal subfield genuinely enlarges the centre", and say "a subalgebra of `ℍ[ℝ]` of degree 2" to match the statement.
findings.issue: The example's docstring draws a general conclusion — "so the maximal subfield of a central division algebra genuinely enlarges the centre; the existence theorem is not answered by `K` itself" — that is false when `deg K D = 1` (take `D = K`: the maximal subfield is `K` = the centre) and is proved here only for `ℍ[ℝ]`. The headline also says "A subfield of `ℍ[ℝ]`" while the statement hypothesizes only `L : Subalgebra ℝ ℍ[ℝ]` with `finrank ℝ L = 2`, nothing about `L` being a field.

findings.evidence: Line 224 vs line 239 `theorem exists_subalgebra_isField_finrank_eq_deg : ∃ L : Subalgebra K D, ...` and line 265 "Worked example: a maximal subfield of the real quaternions".
findings.fix: "### A maximal subfield of a central division algebra", matching the module title and the example heading at line 265.
findings.issue: Section heading "### The maximal subfield of a central division algebra" asserts uniqueness, which is neither true nor proved (ℍ[ℝ] has ℝ⟨i⟩, ℝ⟨j⟩, ... all of degree 2); the file's own theorem is existential and its example docstring at line 273 concedes the subfield is not identified.

findings.evidence: Signature line 292-293 carries `[Nontrivial A] [FiniteDimensional K A]`; proof line 320 `have ha : 0 < finrank K A := Module.finrank_pos`, whose Mathlib statement (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Finite.lean:394) is "A nontrivial finite-dimensional space has positive `finrank`".
findings.fix: Say the count needs `B ⊗[K] Aᵐᵒᵖ` simple plus `A` nonzero and finite-dimensional over `K`, and restrict the line-306 sentence to the algebraic hypotheses (simplicity/centrality).
findings.issue: The docstring advertises the hypothesis set ("asking only for what it uses") but omits `[FiniteDimensional K A]`, and attributes `finrank K A ≠ 0` to nontriviality alone; nontriviality alone does not give it (an infinite-dimensional nontrivial `A` has `finrank K A = 0`). Line 306's "Simplicity of `R` is the only point at which hypotheses on `B` and on `A` enter" is likewise false — finite-dimensionality of `A` enters at `Module.finrank_pos` and at `FiniteDimensional K ↥B`.

summary: Documentation is thorough and its cross-references check out, but three docstrings state more than the code delivers: an example generalizes a quaternion fact into a false general claim, a section heading asserts uniqueness of the maximal subfield, and the new dimension-count docstring misstates its own hypotheses.
